name: Tethba

attributes.attribute: gave her secret name to the lands she loved, now County Westmeath
consort of the king in the land-sovereignty pattern

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Tethba is an Irish goddess or heroine. The record about her is thin. She gave her secret name to the lands she loved. Those lands now form part of County Westmeath, in the Irish midlands. Stories of this kind are told of the land-sovereignty goddess. She was the consort of the king. Her secret name was the key to holding the land. The tale of Tethba fits that older pattern. Little else survives about her.

okr.objective: Record Tethba as an obscure Irish sovereignty goddess.
key_results: Names her link to the lands now in County Westmeath
Places her in the consort-of-the-king sovereignty pattern
